claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake and drop an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, before that execution ever starts.

In a CodePipeline pipeline using `SUPERSEDED` mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, a queued execution waiting behind a running one can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipelineType V2).
Both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` can be set with the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands when defining a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is documented at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the stage interacts with an exclusive lock on the environment it references.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` property is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` running an update.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as it has.
The TeamCity build configuration's advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' has a default of `0` (unlimited).
In TeamCity, the 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is found under the build configuration's General Settings.
With TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
See the update conflicts troubleshooting page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
In Azure Pipelines, serializing Pulumi deployments is done by adding an exclusive lock check to the environment the deployment job targets.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on the stage makes runs waiting on an exclusive lock proceed in sequence.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock' (anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock).
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'Serialize pipeline executions' (anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions).
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'Limit concurrent builds' (anchor #limit-concurrent-builds).
